newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac seeks to up French company takeover defence.
newsitem.headline: Chirac seeks to up French company takeover defence.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said in a magazine interview to appear on Saturday that he had asked the government to prepare legislative changes to improve French company defences against takeovers.

"Compared to our principal competitors, we are at times too exposed and although there is no question of protectionism we should not at the same time be up for sacrifice," Chirac told Valeurs Actuelles.
"So I have asked the government to plan for an overhaul in our takeover legislation."
"There are various channels that could be pursued to better anticipate, better detect attacks -- by giving companies more time to carry out capital increases when under threat," Chirac said.
"We have to strike a balance between normal developments in capital and the need to guard against hostile attacks," he added.

Elaborating on France's corporate health, Chirac said: "It's true that the financial structure of our large companies is not solid enough. They are less heavily capitalised than their competitors and therefore more vulnerable to being taken over by foreigners."
"The important thing is see that our big industrial and financial groups have core shareholder groupings which ensure the stability of the capital and finance for investment" he said.

"That said, the best protection for our companies is profitability, which allows them to bolster their equity funds to invest, finance research and development and buy stakes -- basically to develop," he said.
